name: Annas
overview: Annas and Caiaphas are identified in Scripture as high priests who held significant religious authority during the time of John the Baptist and Jesus' ministry. Luke 3:2 highlights that both were recognized as high priests when the word of God came to John in the wilderness. John 18 records that Jesus was first brought to Annas, who was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, indicating a familial and official connection between these two leaders. Furthermore, Acts 4:6 shows that Annas and Caiaphas, along with their associates, were central figures in the Jerusalem religious leadership. Together, these passages reveal the intertwined roles of Annas and Caiaphas in the priestly hierarchy during a pivotal moment in redemptive history.
